findings.title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil if the user has no topic_users row for this topic. This can happen if the link is opened by a user with no row, for example one who was emailed through mailing list mode or was never tracked. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 instead of being unsubscribed. Use `TopicUser.change`, or create the record when it is missing.

findings.title: State change on a GET request, with no Guardian check
findings.body: A GET action mutates the user's notification level. Link prefetchers, email scanners and CSRF-style image loads can trigger it. Setting a regular-level user to muted is the more harmful case. The action never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!`, and `TopicView.new` is built without the guardian. It should be a POST or PUT, or at least be confirmed by the client page. The bundled Ember route already exposes a UI for changing the state.

findings.title: Toggle semantics are surprising and not idempotent
findings.body: The action lowers tracking/watching to regular, and mutes if the level is already regular or lower. Clicking the same email link twice, or a prefetch followed by a click, silently escalates from 'stop watching' to fully muted. The user message says 'You will stop receiving notifications' without saying which level was applied.

findings.title: Redirect loop or wrong target when slug is blank
findings.body: When the slug doesn't match, the action redirects to `topic.unsubscribe_url`. If the topic's slug is empty (title with only non-slug characters), `url` has an empty segment and the redirect can hit `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` again with a blank slug. That loops forever. The redirect also drops query and format handling.

findings.title: Unsubscribe not covered by tests and `render :show` change affects other callers
findings.body: `perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` explicitly in the html branch. This is needed because the `unsubscribe` action has no template. No controller spec for `unsubscribe` was added, so the nil TopicUser case, the redirect case and the toggle behavior are untested. The spec change only adds an option to an existing builder test.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url missing from templates for non-topic emails
findings.body: `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `send_notification_email` provides it. Any other caller using `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will make I18n raise or leave the literal `%{unsubscribe_url}`. The body then contains a broken link. The spec had to be changed to pass `unsubscribe_url` to avoid this. Provide a fallback, or use a separate translation key when the URL is absent.

findings.title: Multi-line unsubscribe_link yields trailing newline and text-body inconsistency
findings.body: The block scalar `|` appends a trailing newline. In `body`, the unsubscribe text is appended after `"\n"` and now includes two paragraphs. Other locale files that translate `unsubscribe_link` without `%{unsubscribe_url}` will simply omit the per-topic link.

findings.title: Typo in property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.body: The property name is misspelled ('Notificiations'). It is consistently misspelled in the controller and template, so it works, but it is a public name that will be confusing to maintain. Rename it.

findings.title: Triple-stash rendering of a string containing topic title
findings.body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders unescaped HTML. The text is built from `model.fancyTitle`, which is server-escaped. But the translation is interpolated client-side, and anything that bypasses fancy_title escaping would become XSS. This is a risky pattern. Escape the title explicitly and keep the `<strong>` in the template.

findings.title: Title interpolated into HTML unescaped
findings.body: Existing behavior, but the new conditional keeps pushing `title` raw into the buffer. Since `longDescription`, `text` and `row.title` are likewise unescaped, this stays an XSS surface if any of these are user-derived.
